xna-type.name: MouseState
xna-type.summary: This structure is available only when developing for Windows.

constructor.signature: MouseState(Object, Object, Object, Object, Object, Object, Object, Object)
constructor.summary: Initializes a new instance of the MouseState class.
constructor.syntax: 'Declaration Public Sub New ( _ x As Integer, _ y As Integer, _ scrollWheel As Integer, _ leftButton As ButtonState, _ middleButton As ButtonState, _ rightButton As ButtonState, _ xButton1 As ButtonState, _ xButton2 As ButtonState _ )

parameters.parameter: Type: Int32 Mouse scroll wheel value.
Type: ButtonState Left mouse button state.
Type: ButtonState Middle mouse button state.
Type: ButtonState Right mouse button state.

constructor.remarks: Games normally use GetState to get the true mouse state. This constructor is used instead to simulate mouse input for passing within the game's own input subsystem.

property.name: ScrollWheelValue
property.summary: This property is available only when developing for Windows.
property.remarks: Unlike standard Windows and WinForms mouse messages, which report a relative value for the scroll wheel, XNA reports the total scroll wheel value accumulated over the length of a game's execution. To process a wheel movement, you must compare the previous frame's wheel value to the current wheel value.

property.remarks: XBUTTON1 and XBUTTON2 are additional buttons used on many mouse devices, often for forward and backward navigation in Web browsers. They return the same data as standard mouse buttons.
